structured_output.summary: The $33.20 reference is correct: it is Louisiana's refundable earned income credit, 5% of the federal EITC. Under IRC §32, the joint return qualifies for the no-qualifying-children EITC because the 43-year-old head meets the 25–64 age test, which either spouse can satisfy. Earned income from self-employment (about $9,665) is above the 2026 earned income amount of $8,680, and AGI is below the $18,140 joint phase-out threshold, so the federal EITC is the $664 maximum. R.S. 47:297.8 sets the Louisiana credit at 5% for 2019–2030 and refunds any excess over tax, giving $33.20. The engine's derivation matches this, as does stage 1. The 2025 bills to repeal the credit (SB 149, HB 642) or raise it to 10% (HB 133) all stayed in committee, and the statute's history still ends with Acts 2021, No. 453. The 25 models that answered $0 wrongly thought Louisiana has no refundable EITC, no income tax, or that the 20-year-old spouse disqualifies the couple.
